key_insight: A physics-informed machine learning framework can predict laser-weld porosity across different metals by encoding keyhole stability and bubble-capture physics into dimensionless features.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable process-window selection and defect avoidance in high-power laser beam welding of aluminum and steel.
method: Conducted systematic laser beam welding experiments over a broad parameter space to measure porosity ratios.
Used a validated multiphysics simulation to model molten-pool behavior and keyhole dynamics.
Built a universal model from physically meaningful dimensionless variables, with Stokes number and keyhole aspect ratio as top factors.
evidence_signal: The framework achieved a general root mean square error of 1.35 for porosity prediction across metallic systems.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of simulation fidelity and the transferability of the selected physical features to other materials or welding setups.
paper_title: Universal physics-informed machine learning framework for the prediction of porosity defects in high-power laser beam welding with different metallic materials
